definitions: A situation where different predictive models produce conflicting or varying results for the same input or problem.
The extent to which multiple models, often trained on similar data, yield divergent predictions or conclusions.
examples: The model disagreement among the climate simulations highlighted the uncertainty in future temperature predictions.
Researchers observed significant model disagreement when comparing the outputs of various economic forecasting tools.
Addressing model disagreement is crucial for building robust and reliable AI systems.
